item.title: Sri Lanka services expands at higher rate in October 2026: PMI
item.dc:creator: Nirmalie Alahakone
item.description: Driven by improvements in other personal services, with notable contributions from financial services and goods transpor
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka’s services sector expanded at a higher rate in October 2026, according to a Purchasing Managers Index compiled by the central bank, which registered an index value of 62.5, compared to 60.5 the previous month.

“Business Activity expanded, driven primarily by improvements in other personal services, with notable contributions from financial services and goods transportation,” CBSL said.

New businesses increased at a slower rate in October 2026, registering 59.8 from September’s 60.9, reflecting expansions in financial services and other personal services, alongside positive contributions from accommodation, food and beverage services, and transportation of goods.

Employment increased in October, “supported by recruitment across several sub sectors to meet rising operational requirements”.

Backlogs of Work declined in the month, at a higher rate compared to the previous month.

Expectations for Business Activity over the next three months remained positive, CBSL said, supported by anticipated increases in tourist arrivals, and the upcoming festive season.

“However, prevailing global uncertainties continue to pose downside risks to the outlook.” (Colombo/Nov16/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka manufacturing PMI expands in October, driven by anticipated seasonal demand
item.dc:creator: Nirmalie Alahakone
item.description: The New Orders sub-index expanded in driven by the manufacture of textiles and wearing apparel and the food and beverage
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka’s manufacturing sector expanded in October 2026, registering a value of 55.3 on a Purchasing Managers Index compiled by the central bank, from 53.0 the previous month.

“This expansion was broad-based, with all sub-indices remaining above the neutral threshold,” CBSL said, noting the outlook remains favourable, underpinned by anticipated demand during the upcoming festive season.

The New Orders sub-index expanded in the month, registering 52.2, driven by the manufacture of textiles and wearing apparel and the food and beverages sectors, reflecting seasonal demand.

The Production sub-index registered 51.0, driven by seasonal demand in the textiles and wearing apparel sector.

The Employment sub-index expanded at a slower rate, registering 51.1, from the previous 52.6.

The Stock of Purchases sub-index also expanded from the neutral threshold, registering 56.1.

Suppliers’ Delivery Times sub-index further lengthened during the period, reflecting increased demand for inputs. (Colombo/Nov16/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka stocks close down 1.32-pct amid profit-taking
item.dc:creator: Ranul Seneviratne
item.description: Turnover Rs10.48bn
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka’s Colombo Stock Exchange closed down on Monday, CSE data showed, with the benchmark All Share Price Index moving down 1.32 percent.

The ASPI was down 291.81 points at 21,732.37, while the more liquid S&P SL20 was down 1.50 percent, or 94.69 points, at 6,199.03.

“More than the budget, what we need to factor in is that the market had been going at a very rapid pace for quite some time,” Raynal Wickremeratne, Head of Research and Strategy at NDB Securities, said.

“Every time the market moves at that speed, there tends to be a period where things slow down a little bit and there is some profit-taking. You actually need a few corrections to have a healthy market.”

Positive contributors to the ASPI were Carson Cumberbatch (up 0.35 percent at 707.75 rupees), Bukit Darah (up 0.53 percent at 859.50 rupees), Citizens Development Business Finance (up 0.90 percent at 33.80 rupees), HNB Life (up 2.19 percent at 140 rupees), and InsureMe Insurance Brokers (up 11.12 percent at 3,045.25 rupees).

Commercial Bank (down 1.55 percent at 221.75 rupees), Dialog Axiata (down 1.20 percent at 49.60 rupees), Hatton National Bank (down 0.99 percent at 399.75 rupees), Tokyo Cement Company (Lanka) (down 4.99 percent at 83.80 rupees), and LOLC Finance (down 5.77 percent at 4.90 rupees) were top negative contributors.

Market turnover was 10.48 billion rupees. Food and staples retailing led turnover with 4.51 billion rupees.

Turnover was bolstered by a major on-board transaction of 4.4 billion rupees in Carson Cumberbatch, alongside several crossings. The largest crossing was recorded in Convenience Foods (Lanka) at 3.976 billion rupees, followed by Dialog Axiata (140 million rupees), Hemas Holdings (41 million rupees), Prime Lands Residencies (30 million rupees), and Aitken Spence (22 million rupees).

item.title: Softlogic Holdings Sept quarter net loss narrows 25-pct to Rs2.1bn
item.dc:creator: Ranul Seneviratne
item.description: Healthcare anchored earnings, with revenue rising 24 percent to Rs. 10.64 billion and pre-tax profit jumping 80 percent
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT — Sri Lanka conglomerate Softlogic Holdings PLC recorded a net loss attributable to equity holders of Rs. 2.10 billion for the quarter ended September 30, narrowing 25 percent from a loss of Rs. 2.79 billion a year earlier, interim accounts showed.

Basic loss per share improved to Rs. 1.50 from Rs. 2.00 in the same quarter last year.

Quarterly revenue rose 15 percent to Rs. 34.85 billion from Rs. 30.17 billion, outpacing a 12 percent rise in cost of sales to Rs. 22.25 billion and lifting gross profit 22 percent to Rs. 12.60 billion.

Operating profit surged 97 percent to Rs. 3.62 billion, with EBITDA climbing 68 percent to Rs. 4.59 billion, supported by tight administrative expense growth of 3 percent (Rs. 8.17 billion) despite a 27 percent rise in distribution costs to Rs. 1.46 billion.

Healthcare anchored earnings, with revenue rising 24 percent to Rs. 10.64 billion and pre-tax profit jumping 80 percent to Rs. 2.49 billion on higher finance income.

Retail revenue grew 22 percent to Rs. 9.52 billion, though Rs. 1.71 billion in finance costs widened its pre-tax loss to Rs. 2.03 billion.

Information technology swung to a Rs. 181.3 million pre-tax profit and leisure pre-tax losses narrowed 88 percent to Rs. 79.5 million, while automobile revenue fell 57 percent to Rs. 494.6 million.

Financial services revenue increased 15 percent to Rs. 11.76 billion with operating profit up 11 percent to Rs. 1.22 billion, but the segment posted a Rs. 365.7 million pre-tax loss (versus a Rs. 1.28 billion profit previously) after insurance contract liability charges jumped 194 percent to Rs. 2.81 billion.

Notes showed no life insurance surplus was transferred to shareholders during the quarter, compared to Rs. 1.26 billion a year earlier.

Group net finance costs fell 17 percent to Rs. 1.26 billion following Rs. 2.03 billion in rights issue debt repayments. Currency translation of foreign operations had minimal impact, yielding a Rs. 3.19 million gain alongside a Rs. 242.2 million derivative fair value gain.

After Rs. 937.4 million in taxes, total group loss narrowed 7 percent to Rs. 1.40 billion.

Total assets stood at Rs. 212.86 billion with negative net asset value of Rs. 51.36 per share and Rs. 7.63 billion in capital commitments, while subsidiary Asiri Surgical continues litigating a Rs. 1.20 billion BOI tax dispute.

Post-quarter, Softlogic Finance approved a Rs. 1.00 billion rights issue to expand vehicle financing, Softlogic Life announced plans to amalgamate Softlogic Life Insurance Lanka from January 1, 2027, and the parent extended warrant conversion payments to November 19.

Softlogic Holdings’ shares closed at 7.10 rupees at the end of September. The share is currently trading around 9.60 rupees.  (Colombo/Nov16/2026)

item.title: South Korea, Sri Lanka discuss ageing populations, investment
item.dc:creator: Nirmalie Alahakone
item.description: Declining fertility rates and a rapidly ageing population that threaten future dependency ratios and workforce availabil
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – A visiting South Korean parliamentary delegation has held talks with Sri Lanka’s Deputy Speaker Rizvie Salih on tackling demographic shifts, climate resilience, and boosting corporate participation ahead of the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations in 2027.

The delegation from the National Assembly of the Republic of Korea, representing the Korean Parliamentary League on Children, Population and Environment (CPE), committed to encouraging greater participation by Korean enterprises in Sri Lanka’s forthcoming international expo scheduled for January next year, a parliament statement said.

Led by Lee Yang-soo, Chairperson of the National Assembly Intelligence Committee and Vice President of the CPE, the delegation also invited Sri Lanka’s parliament to attend the Asia-Pacific Parliamentarians’ Conference on Environment and Development (APPCED) in South Korea next year.

Both sides noted that natural disasters can undermine years of economic progress and stressed the need to balance environmental protection with economic growth.

Salih flagged Sri Lanka’s own demographic pressures, pointing to declining fertility rates and a rapidly ageing population that threaten future dependency ratios and workforce availability, alongside challenges in sustaining the country’s free education system.

The Korean lawmakers shared South Korea’s policy interventions aimed at reversing low birth rates, including affordable rental housing for newlyweds, low-interest loans, and housing incentives.

They also discussed proposals to raise the retirement age from 60 to 65 to bridge pension coverage gaps while safeguarding youth employment opportunities.

The two sides discussed expanding bilateral tourism — buoyed by the growing popularity of K-pop in Sri Lanka — and noted the economic benefits of technical and vocational training gained by Sri Lankan youth working in South Korea.

The Korean delegation included CPE member Kwak Sang-eon, Korea-Sri Lanka Parliamentary Friendship Association Vice President Kim So-hee, and South Korean Ambassador to Sri Lanka Youn-Jung Kim. Secretary General of Parliament Kushani Rohanadeera also attended the meeting. (Colombo/Nov16/2026)

item.title: Abans Sept quarter net profit falls 28-pct to Rs791mn on finance costs
item.dc:creator: Ranul Seneviratne
item.description: Surging borrowing costs and weaker associate earnings outweighed strong top-line growth
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT — Sri Lanka consumer durables and financial services group Abans PLC recorded a net profit of Rs. 790.6 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, down 28.4 percent from Rs. 1.10 billion a year earlier, as surging borrowing costs and weaker associate earnings outweighed strong top-line growth.

Basic earnings per share declining to Rs. 0.31 from Rs. 0.46, interim accounts showed.

Quarterly revenue jumped 30.8 percent to Rs. 19.81 billion from Rs. 15.15 billion, propelled by robust demand across its core trading and financial services operations.

Cost of sales rose at a slower 27.2 percent to Rs. 12.37 billion, lifting gross profit 37.2 percent to Rs. 7.44 billion and widening gross margins to 37.6 percent from 35.8 percent.

However, operating profit growth moderated to 25.5 percent, reaching Rs. 2.02 billion compared to Rs. 1.61 billion previously, as selling and distribution expenses surged 53.2 percent to Rs. 3.08 billion and administrative costs rose 29.5 percent to Rs. 2.44 billion amid retail expansion and higher warranty provisions.

Net profit was dragged down below the operating line by a 63.8 percent spike in finance costs to Rs. 998.7 million (from Rs. 609.8 million) and a 25.7 percent drop in finance income to Rs. 147.9 million.

Group interest-bearing borrowings expanded 45.3 percent from March 2026 to Rs. 38.41 billion — led by a 51.1 percent jump in short-term debt to Rs. 30.84 billion — to fund a 43.8 percent inventory buildup to Rs. 26.21 billion and higher receivables.

Share of profits from equity-accounted investees, Abans Electricals PLC and Colombo City Centre, plunged 62.7 percent to Rs. 103.3 million from Rs. 277.2 million.

Pre-tax profit declined 17.4 percent to Rs. 1.13 billion after financial services value-added tax rose 34.6 percent to Rs. 136.1 million, while income tax expense climbed 28.0 percent to Rs. 342.3 million.

Notes to the accounts disclosed a Rs. 1 billion term loan borrowed from associate Abans Electricals PLC, Rs. 1.34 billion raised in listed debentures via Abans Finance PLC, and a Rs. 466 million surcharge tax provision for 2020/21 settled after September 30. No new business ventures were announced.

Total group assets crossed Rs. 101.76 billion, with net asset value per share at Rs. 12.94 and debt-to-equity at 1.24 times. Abans PLC’s ordinary shares are not publicly traded, being wholly owned by Abans Retail Holdings (Pvt) Ltd. (Colombo/Nov16/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka taxman to issue valuation rules for crypto and gems under expanded capital gains tax
item.dc:creator: Ranul Seneviratne
item.description: The 2027 budget proposes adding digital and virtual assets — including cryptocurrencies — alongside telecom and broadcas
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka’s Inland Revenue Department (IRD) will introduce formal valuation guidelines for calculating capital gains tax on cryptocurrencies, broadcast licenses, gems, and real estate after the 2027 budget expanded the tax net to cover digital and intangible assets.

Speaking at a Deloitte Sri Lanka post-budget webinar, IRD Senior Deputy Commissioner Nihal Wijewardena admitted that the lack of official valuation rules has caused widespread disputes over the September 30, 2017 baseline market value even for land and buildings.

Under existing tax law, capital gains tax applies mainly to land, buildings, and company shares, taxed at a concessionary 15 percent rate for individuals and 30 percent for companies.

The 2027 budget proposes adding digital and virtual assets — including cryptocurrencies — alongside telecom and broadcasting licenses, gems, jewelry, and precious metals to the definition of taxable capital assets.

Wijewardena said the upcoming tax amendment will give the Commissioner General legal authority to set clear valuation methods for each asset class.

“Definitely this time the provision will grant power to the Commissioner to issue a specific guideline when the amendment act is in operation,” Wijewardena said.

Tax practitioners at the forum noted that valuing volatile virtual assets or historic intangible rights could be even harder than pricing property unless clear rules are published before enforcement begins.

Wijewardena also clarified new anti-avoidance rules proposed for corporate amalgamations and mergers.

Currently, Sri Lanka’s tax laws contain no specific provisions governing company mergers, creating uncertainty over whether merged firms can carry forward past business losses.

While business groups raised concerns that anti-avoidance rules could penalize legitimate corporate restructurings, Wijewardena said the department aims to protect genuine commercial mergers as tax-neutral transactions while blocking artificial group arrangements designed solely to absorb tax losses.

“If the first reason for the amalgamation is business we can accept, if the first reason is tax avoidance then those should be answered,” he said.

Deloitte panelists urged the tax authority to consult the private sector before drafting the merger rules so complex business deals are not accidentally blocked.

Meanwhile, Wijewardena acknowledged that clearing overdue income tax refunds remains the single most important service standard the public should hold the IRD accountable for in 2027.

Following the abolition of the Simplified Value Added Tax (SVAT) system and the launch of a risk-based refund mechanism, the department cut average refund processing times to 29 days—against a 45-day legal limit—and cleared 7 billion rupees in decade-old arrears.

The 2027 budget also grants new export-oriented firms with at least 80 percent export turnover access to the fast-track VAT refund scheme after six months of registration, while giving legal recognition to electronic tax invoices. (Colombo/Nov16/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka’s new active credit card up 1-pct in September
item.dc:creator: Shihar Aneez
item.description: New active cards have expanded by 7.1% in first nine months of 2026
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – The expansion in new active credit cards in Sri Lanka saw 1 percent growth in September, official data showed.

New active credit cards in September recorded an increase of 22,011, the Central Bank’s latest data showed.

The total number of active credit cards reached 2,319,794 by the end of September.

The number has expanded 7.1 percent or 153,608 in the first nine months of this year.

Active credit cards rose 7.8 percent (157,730) in 2025, following a 4.8 percent (91,371) rise in 2024. This growth was driven by the island nation’s economic recovery and strong credit card promotions amid falling interest rates.

However, the Central Bank reversed its dovish monetary policy and raised the key monetary policy rate by 100 basis points in May. After the tightening, the island nation saw a slowdown in credit card growth in June.

In May, active credit cards recorded an increase of 25,720. The Central Bank tightened the monetary policy in the last week of May.

With the tight monetary policy and fuel rationing since March, people may not be spending as much as they spent before that, analysts said.

Sri Lanka’s economic recovery and stability have helped customers to use more credit since 2023.

Some analysts noted that higher interest (penalty) rates on credit cards also prompted some users to cancel their cards after the economic crisis and those same customers might now be actively using the cards due to declining rates.

Active credit cards fell 1.8% (39,991) in 2023 after country declared bankruptcy in 2022 amid an unprecedented hike in the Central Bank’s monetary policy rates.

The central bank sharply increased interest rates in April 2022 to fight hyperinflation.

However, the inflation slowed to a deflation September 2024 before turning to positive in August last year amid the central bank’s reduction of key policy rates eight times since June 2023.

The Central Bank’s policy tightening cycle started after the inflation jumped in April following sharp rupee depreciation and higher inflation following the fuel price hikes. (Colombo/Novembber 15/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka’s monthly tourism revenue up 3.5-pct in October 2026
item.dc:creator: Shihar Aneez
item.description: Total revenue in first 10 months still down 8.3 percent to US$2,437.9mn
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka’s monthly foreign exchange revenue from tourism rose for a third straight month in October 2026 and gained 3.5 percent from a year ago to US$192.7 million, the central bank said, quoting tourism promotion authority data.

The rise comes with a 2.1 percent rise in monthly tourist arrivals last month, data showed.

Tourism revenue has fallen since October 2025 with the government-owned tourism promotion body’s revision of the daily average spending per tourist and the duration of the tourist stay.

Total tourism revenue in the first 10 months still down 8.3 percent to US$2,437.9 million, compared to US$2,659.0 million in the same period last year.

Arrivals in the first 10 months showed a 1.5 percent decline.

The island nation recorded its lowest revenue in 32 months in June this year. Tourism revenue has been falling rapidly year-on-year since the U.S./Israel bombing of Iran began on February 28.

The state-owned Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA) revised the methodology for compiling monthly tourism earnings estimates in May this year, retrospectively from January, citing the need to “enhance the accuracy and representativeness”.

Sri Lanka has revised down its ambitious arrival target to 2.7 million from 3 million and the revenue goal to US$4.2 billion from US$5 billion for this year.

The island nation witnessed US$3.22 billion in revenue in 2025, a 1.6 percent jump compared to US$3.17 billion in the previous year, according to the data.

Arrivals picked up 15.1 percent in 2025 compared to the previous year, with the number of foreign visitors to Sri Lanka rising to a record 2,362,521 from 2,053,465.

Tourism accounted for nearly 5 percent of Sri Lanka’s economy when the sector was at its peak in 2018. Since then, the sector has been hit by the violent Easter Sunday suicide attack in 2019, the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020, followed by an unprecedented economic crisis.

The Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority estimates the tourism earnings figure from a survey.

Sri Lanka’s imports and the merchandise trade deficit have gradually picked up as tourism earnings came in and people in the sector spent their wages and other earnings. (Colombo/November 15/2026)

item.title: Foreign investors dump Sri Lanka rupee bonds for fourth straight week
item.dc:creator: Shihar Aneez
item.description: The selling extended net foreign outflows from the rupee bonds to Rs33.9bn in last six weeks.
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Foreign investors sold Sri Lanka rupee bonds and exited from the island nation’s risk-free assets for a fourth straight week in the week ended on November 12, Central Bank data showed, amid depreciation in the rupee currency.

With the latest outflows, the island nation has seen net foreign selling in six out of the last 21 weeks.

Offshore investors sold a net Rs. 5,447 million (US$16.5 million) worth of Sri Lanka rupee bonds in the week ended on November 12.

The net selling extended the net foreign outflows from the rupee bonds to Rs. 33.9 billion in the last six weeks.

Despite outflows in the last four weeks, the island nation has seen a total inflow of around Rs. 38.2 billion into local currency bonds this year through Nov 12, following a net inflow of 71.5 billion rupees last year.

The latest foreign selling comes after the U.S. mid-term election showed strong checks and balances for Trump’s presidential powers and hopes of an end to hostilities against Iran. It also came as the Israel Prime Minister failed to secure a majority in his election.

The rupee had been steady for more than three years before the sharp depreciation in May with the Central Bank citing higher oil and vehicle imports amid a lingering conflict in the Middle East.

The rupee has fallen 6.8 percent through November 13, this year.

Globally, investors are cautious about economic growth due to the impact of the latest Middle East escalation.

The rupee has stabilized after the Central Bank raised its key monetary policy rate by 100 basis points in May to curb inflationary pressure stemming from higher demand.

The island nation has seen an uptick in inflation in the last seven months following a nearly 50 percent hike in fuel prices.

The government raised fuel prices in the last week of October, raising further inflationary concerns.

Before the May rate hike, the Central Bank kept its key policy rates steady since May 2025 after reducing them by 825 basis points over 24 months since June 2023 and foreign investors have been buying rupee bonds. (Colombo/November 14/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka picked for first time in Four Seasons 2028 private jet tour
item.dc:creator: Ranul Seneviratne
item.description: 48 guests will spend three nights in Sri Lanka from May 12 to May 15.
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka has been picked for the first time as a stop on a Four Seasons Private Jet Experience, with the global luxury hospitality group adding the island to its new 2028 around-the-world itinerary.

The 23-day journey, named Coastlines & Culture, will run in May 2028 and carry up to 48 guests across eight destinations. Guests will spend three nights in Sri Lanka from May 12 to May 15.

Because Four Seasons does not operate a hotel in Sri Lanka, travellers will stay at Cape Weligama, an independent property selected for the stop, according to the company’s announcement.

“Curating a new Private Jet itinerary requires immense thought and care,” Marc Speichert, Executive Vice President and Chief Commercial Officer at Four Seasons, said.

During the Sri Lanka leg, guests will visit a private Ceylon cinnamon estate to see how the spice is harvested and turned into quills and oil, followed by lunch overlooking the hills.

Optional trips include seeing elephants at Udawalawe National Park, taking a private flight to UNESCO-listed Dambulla and Sigiriya Rock, or touring Galle Fort and tasting local spirit arrack.

“With Coastlines & Culture, we’re able to bring together destinations rarely experienced within a single journey, creating moments of awe and discovery,” he added.

The tour is priced from 238,000 US dollars (around 212,200 euros) per person based on double occupancy, with a single supplement of 23,800 US dollars.

Guests will fly aboard a custom-configured Airbus A321neo-LR aircraft operated by Titan Airways Limited and run by TCS World Travel. A dedicated journey team, including a concierge, executive chef, and physician, will accompany passengers throughout the trip.

Aside from Sri Lanka, the eight-stop route covers San Francisco, Seoul, Hangzhou, Zanzibar, Sharm El Sheikh, Cap-Ferrat, and Hampshire. (Colombo/Nov14/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka budget ignores provincial polls while stripping council powers: MP
item.dc:creator: Nirmalie Alahakone
item.description: "About the Provincial elections, you haven't mentioned a word, but what have you mentioned? You are taking away the powe
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – A Sri Lankan opposition legislator has criticized the government’s 2027 budget speech for failing to mention or allocate provisions for long-delayed Provincial Council elections, while accusing the administration of stripping away devolved powers.

“Previous governments had a policy on their policy statement: they would mention the Provincial Council elections,” Illankai Tamil Arasu Kachchi (ITAK) MP Shanakiyan Rasamanickam told parliament during the budget debate.

“Not a single word about the Provincial Council election! About the Provincial elections, you haven’t mentioned a word, but what have you mentioned? You are taking away the powers of the Provincial Council.”

Rasamanickam pointed out that the government was taking over six provincial hospitals — Mullaitivu, Mannar, Kilinochchi, Vavuniya, Avissawella, and Gampaha — while continuing to delay the polls.

The 2027 national budget presented by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake proposed to transfer to
the central Government the District General Hospitals of Mannar, Mullaitivu, Vavuniya, Kilinochchi, Gampaha and Avissawella, which are administered by the Provincial Councils, out of the 20 District General Hospitals.

“You are taking away power that was given to the Provincial Council, whilst not having Provincial Council elections,” he said.

“Last year, powers given to the provinces regarding environmental policies — you’ve taken it back, with no consent of the Provincial Council.”

He also criticized the budget speech for making no mention of land release issues in the North and East, a new constitution, or the government’s pledge to abolish the executive presidency.

“In this budget, I must also mention, not only the Provincial Council election, about the new constitution — not a single word about the constitution! What is happening to your plans and proposals of abolishing the executive presidency? Where is the new constitution?” Rasamanickam questioned.

The legislator further raised concerns over proposed legislation, including the Protection of the State from Terrorism Act (PSTA) and the Organized Crime Bill, arguing they were more repressive than the existing Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA) they are meant to replace.

“The trajectory of this government is worrying to me. It’s really worrying to me,” Rasamanickam said.
“Because if the objective is to say that there is no Tamil national question, if the objective is to say that you all have resolved any ethnic issue that this country faced, then I think the Tamil people will teach this government a very, very, very harsh lesson in the future.” (Colombo/Nov13/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka MP slams budget speech for omitting Tamil national question
item.dc:creator: Nirmalie Alahakone
item.description: "A budget speech generally, is a policy direction of the government for the next year.
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – A Sri Lanka legislator has voiced strong disappointment that the President’s budget speech failed to make a single mention of the Tamil national question.

“It is very unfortunate that in His Excellency the President’s speech, there has not been a single word mentioned about the Tamil national question. Not a single word,” Shanakiyan Rasamanickam said.

“A budget speech generally, is a policy direction of the government for the next year. The budget speech is not only a statement of the country’s fiscal position or the economy’s position. It is the country’s, the government’s, plan, or what the government plans to do the following year. That’s a policy statement.”

Former presidents would at least mention the Tamil question even if it was not resolved, he said.

Former President Ranil Wickremesinghe in his speech, in his policy statement, he would mention: “The Tamil national question must be resolved,” Rasamanickam said.

Former Presidents Maithripala Sirisena and Gotabaya Rajapaksa also mentioned that the national ethnic question must be resolved, he added.

“Every President, every country’s Head of State, in their policy statements, have acknowledged the fact that there is an unresolved national issue, the Tamil national question, that it needs to be resolved. Various governments have proposed various mechanisms; none of them have succeeded, but at least it was mentioned.”

This year’s budget made allocations for the Office of Missing Persons, and the Office of Reparations.

“But the domestic mechanism is a mechanism that the victim community has rejected. So you all are allocating money to a mechanism where the victim community is not going to be part of.”

Last year’s budget 1 billion was allocated to be spent on the Trincomalee and Jaffna airports.

“Where was that 1 billion for the Trincomalee and Jaffna airports spent last year?”

“The trajectory of this government, Honourable Deputy Speaker, is worrying to me. It’s really worrying to me. Because if the objective is to say that there is no Tamil national question, if the objective is to say that you all have resolved any ethnic issue that this country faced, then Honourable Deputy Speaker, then I think the Tamil people will teach this government a very, very, very harsh lesson in the future.” (Colombo/Nov13/2026)

item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka has sold 6,500 million rupees of treasury bills offered on tap at an average rate of 9.95 percent, the public debt management office said, bringing the total of bills sold in the week to 85.562 billion rupees.

item.title: Access Engineering Sept quarter group net profit surges 200-pct to Rs4.75bn
item.dc:creator: Ranul Seneviratne
item.description: Underpinned by condominium property handovers alongside strong automobile sales and steady civil engineering execution
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT — Sri Lanka’s Access Engineering PLC recorded a group net profit attributable to equity holders of Rs. 4.75 billion for the quarter ended September 30, surging 200 percent from Rs. 1.58 billion a year earlier, interim accounts showed.

Basic earnings per share rose to Rs. 4.08 for the September quarter, up from Rs. 1.58 previously.

Quarterly group revenue expanded 36 percent to Rs. 20.39 billion from Rs. 14.94 billion, underpinned by condominium property handovers — reflected in inventories dropping Rs. 7.69 billion since March to Rs. 35.71 billion — alongside strong automobile sales and steady civil engineering execution.

Cost of sales rose at a slower 27 percent to Rs. 14.34 billion, lifting gross profit by 64 percent to Rs. 6.05 billion and expanding gross margins to 29.7 percent from 24.7 percent.

Other income jumped 144 percent to Rs. 259.9 million, while administrative expenses rose 75 percent to Rs. 1.14 billion, leaving operating profit up 64 percent at Rs. 5.16 billion.

However, finance costs more than doubled, rising 107 percent to Rs. 1.18 billion on elevated group borrowings of Rs. 43.74 billion, partly offset by finance income climbing 302 percent to Rs. 42.2 million.

Share of results from equity-accounted investees rose 122 percent to Rs. 26.7 million, pushing pre-tax profit up 56 percent to Rs. 4.05 billion.

Income tax swung to a net reversal of Rs. 186.6 million from an expense of Rs. 804.1 million, boosted by deferred tax assets on unrelieved losses from a 100 percent enhanced capital allowance claimed by 60 percent-owned radiopharmaceutical subsidiary Access Medical Tracers (Private) Limited.

Total period profit rose 136 percent to Rs. 4.24 billion, with non-controlling interest declining 24 percent to Rs. 164.9 million following last year’s buyout of minority shareholders in Harbour Village (Private) Limited.

No separate exchange gain or loss was itemized in quarterly earnings, though foreign currency translation via associates recorded a Rs. 17.4 million loss in other comprehensive income, alongside USD 16.6 million in corporate guarantees.

Notes also flagged an expected Rs. 1.45 billion recovery from the terminated South Asia Commercial and Logistics Hub project, a Rs. 225 million post-quarter legal settlement already provided for, and a Supreme Court appeal over a 2011/12 PAYE tax ruling.

Group assets stood at Rs. 132.4 billion as of September 30, with net asset value per share at Rs. 46.70, as the Employees’ Provident Fund raised its stake to 5.69 percent.

Access Engineering shares closed at 80.00 rupees at the end of September and are currently trading around 85.80 rupees. (Colombo/Nov13/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka private sector says timely implementation of Budget 2027 key
item.dc:creator: Nirmalie Alahakone
item.description: More targeted and actionable proposals could have been introduced to unlock potential of sectors with significant growth
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Private sector body, The Ceylon Chamber of Commerce, said it was encouraged by the broad direction of Budget 2027, noting that it reinforces Sri Lanka’s commitment to economic transformation while maintaining policy continuity, macroeconomic stability, and fiscal discipline.

“This continuity is particularly important as the country seeks to transition from economic stabilisation to a more durable, investment-led growth trajectory.”

The chamber also noted several areas where the Budget could have placed greater emphasis to strengthen the country’s growth prospects.

“In particular, there is a need for a stronger focus on attracting Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), accelerating factor market reforms, particularly in land and labour, and fast-tracking public procurement reforms to improve the efficiency and speed of project implementation.

“More targeted and actionable proposals could have been introduced to unlock the potential of sectors with significant growth opportunities, including tourism, agriculture, IT/BPO and logistics.”

The chamber said the budget contains positive measures aimed at enhancing competitiveness, and external sector resilience, while presenting opportunities for focus on sectors that can accelerate growth.

“A number of the key structural reforms identified in last year’s Budget have been carried forward and strengthened, providing greater certainty and predictability to businesses and investors.

“These include the continued implementation of the Trade National Single Window (TNSW), the phased removal of para-tariffs, the rollout of the Digital ID framework, efforts to expand market access through new Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), the strengthening of one-stop-shop investment facilitation mechanisms, progress on Customs reforms, the expansion of Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA), enhanced financing support for SMEs, and reforms relating to the management of State-Owned Enterprises.”

The CCC said that more than 20 proposals submitted by it have been reflected in Budget 2027.

These include measures to strengthen investor facilitation through the establishment of a professionally managed investment promotion agency; continued efforts to improve trade facilitation and export competitiveness; the Government’s consideration of a successor programme with the International Monetary Fund (IMF); accelerated progress on key legislative reforms; the expansion of digital government services; and the promotion of cashless payments and broader digital adoption. The Budget has also captured several priorities relating to energy security, including the accelerated deployment of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and investments in fuel storage infrastructure, initiatives to optimize underutilized agricultural land, measures to support the expansion of the digital economy and the IT/BPO sector, and tax reforms to support exporters, including the acceptance of newly VAT-registered exporters as eligible exporters.

“The inclusion of these priorities reflects the value of sustained public-private dialogue and demonstrates increasing alignment between national policy objectives and the needs of a competitive, export-oriented economy.

“The priority now must be effective and timely implementation to translate policy commitments into investment, competitiveness, exports and sustainable growth.” (Colombo/Nov13/2026)
